verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Both clauses are stated, in the logarithmic radial coordinate rather than in the symbols I, X, H. Clause 1: by (4.15) I(X) = ∫_0^X H dx with H = √(2x)E (p24 symbol table, p28 display); substituting x = e^t, dx = e^t dt turns I(X_end) into ∫_{t≤Y} e^t √(2 e^t) E(t,η) dt and XH/(1−λ) into e^Y √(2 e^Y) E(Y,η)/(1−λ), which is exactly `physical_integral_endpoint` (its own docstring states the dictionary 'X = exp y and H = sqrt (2*X) * E'). The improper lower limit is handled by `history_from_ideal_prefix` (line 1284), which uses the (A.7) ideal prefix E = P f(η) e^{y/10} and contributes (5/8)·P·shape η. Clause 2: Lean integrates (E² − E_unedited²) over all of ℝ (`pressure_neutral`) or over 0..releaseStart (`pressure_interval_neutral`) instead of over 'the two bumps'; these agree with the paper's integral because the integrand vanishes off Ioo (releaseStart − 4, releaseStart) (`correctedAngular_unchanged`, line 1072, via `relative_support` ⊆ Icc (−3/20) (43/20)), which is the window holding the two width-.3 bumps centred three and one units before releaseStart. The 'end' is `d.releaseStart = d.flattenEnd + 30 log(1/λ)`, matching the paper's 30 log(1/λ) interval.
